text: Where does a payment system start, if not with payments?
prefix: Where does a payment system start, if not with payments?

text: It starts with a project that builds, and an environment that runs with one command.
prefix: It starts with a project that builds, and an environment that runs with one command.

text: We use Java twenty-five and Spring Boot four, with Gradle builds written in Groovy, the way the bank writes its own.
prefix: We use Java twenty-five and Spring Boot four, with Gradle builds written in Groovy, the way the bank writes its own.

text: The app has five modules, partner, commission, terminal, card, and payment, and each one owns its own schema, with a database user that can see nothing else.
prefix: The app has five modules, partner, commission, terminal, card, and payment, and each one owns its own schema, with a database user that can see nothing else.

text: A module talks to another only through the public interface in its root package, and the build fails if it reaches any further.
prefix: A module talks to another only through the public interface in its root package, and the build fails if it reaches any further.

text: Shared pieces live in a platform folder, each its own build, published to the local Maven repository.
prefix: Shared pieces live in a platform folder, each its own build, published to the local Maven repository.

text: The version catalog pins every version, so the build is the same on every machine.
prefix: The version catalog pins every version, so the build is the same on every machine.

text: Errors follow one format: each module lists its errors in an enum, and a YAML file gives each one its HTTP status and its message in English, Russian and Uzbek.
prefix: Errors follow one format: each module lists its errors in an enum, and a YAML file gives each one its HTTP status and its message in English, Russian and Uzbek.

text: API contracts are OpenAPI files, and the code generated from them lives only in the published jars, never in our source.
prefix: API contracts are OpenAPI files, and the code generated from them lives only in the published jars, never in our source.

text: Every module follows the same layers, controller, service, repository, and entity, with its constants in one place.
prefix: Every module follows the same layers, controller, service, repository, and entity, with its constants in one place.

text: Services that do one job live outside the app, each with its own contract and client: the card scheme adapters, and the file service.
prefix: Services that do one job live outside the app, each with its own contract and client: the card scheme adapters, and the file service.

text: A separate infrastructure repository uses Docker Compose to start Postgres and Redis, and every other tool joins only when a problem needs it.
prefix: A separate infrastructure repository uses Docker Compose to start Postgres and Redis, and every other tool joins only when a problem needs it.

text: With one setting, the app logs structured JSON in the community ECS format, and reports its health from the very first minute.
prefix: With one setting, the app logs structured JSON in the community ECS format, and reports its health from the very first minute.

text: One command in the infrastructure repository, and the whole world is up.
prefix: One command in the infrastructure repository, and the whole world is up.

text: The code, the infrastructure, the load tests, and the web app each live in their own repository.
prefix: The code, the infrastructure, the load tests, and the web app each live in their own repository.
